claim: The static structure of the nuclear pore complex (NPC) continues to be refined with cryo-EM and x-ray crystallography.
source: While the static structure of the nuclear pore complex (NPC) continues to be refined with cryo-EM and x-ray crystallography, in vivo conformational changes of the NPC remain under-explored.
evidence: This is a general statement about ongoing structural biology work on NPCs, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: In vivo conformational changes of the NPC remain under-explored.
source: While the static structure of the nuclear pore complex (NPC) continues to be refined with cryo-EM and x-ray crystallography, in vivo conformational changes of the NPC remain under-explored.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current knowledge about NPC dynamics in living cells.

claim: Sensors that report on the orientation of NPC components were developed by rigidly conjugating mEGFP to different NPC proteins.
source: We developed sensors that report on the orientation of NPC components by rigidly conjugating mEGFP to different NPC proteins.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach developed in this study.

claim: Select domains of nucleoporins within the inner ring (Nup54, Nup58, Nup62) undergo conformational changes when transport through the NPC is perturbed.
source: Our studies show conformational changes to select domains of nucleoporins (Nups) within the inner ring (Nup54, Nup58, Nup62) when transport through the NPC is perturbed and no conformational changes to Nups elsewhere in the NPC.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the figures.

claim: No conformational changes occur to Nups elsewhere in the NPC when transport is perturbed.
source: Our studies show conformational changes to select domains of nucleoporins (Nups) within the inner ring (Nup54, Nup58, Nup62) when transport through the NPC is perturbed and no conformational changes to Nups elsewhere in the NPC.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data showing no changes in Nup133 and Nup93 orientations.

claim: Select components of the NPC are flexible and undergo conformational changes upon engaging with cargo.
source: Our results suggest that select components of the NPC are flexible and undergo conformational changes upon engaging with cargo.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results presented in the study.

claim: The scaffold of the NPC is a cylindrical channel composed of proteins that form an eight-spoked core with an axis perpendicular to the nuclear envelope.
source: The scaffold of the NPC is a cylindrical channel composed of proteins that form an eight-spoked core with an axis perpendicular to the nuclear envelope (Alber et al., 2007; Kim et al., 2018; Kosinski et al., 2016; Mosalaganti et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about NPCs supported by multiple citations.

claim: NPCs are composed of ~30 distinct proteins called nucleoporins (Nups) represented in 8, 16, or 32-fold copy number.
source: NPCs are composed of ~30 distinct proteins called nucleoporins (Nups) represented in 8, 16, or 32-fold copy number.
evidence: This is established knowledge about NPC composition.

claim: An individual yeast NPC is composed of ~500 Nups for a total mass of ~66 MDa.
source: An individual yeast NPC is composed of ~500 Nups for a total mass of ~66 MDa (Rout and Blobel, 1993), whereas a vertebrate NPC has ~1000 total Nups (Hoelz et al., 2011) fpr a tptal mass of ~109 MDa (Reichelt et al., 1990).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: A vertebrate NPC has ~1000 total Nups for a total mass of ~109 MDa.
source: An individual yeast NPC is composed of ~500 Nups for a total mass of ~66 MDa (Rout and Blobel, 1993), whereas a vertebrate NPC has ~1000 total Nups (Hoelz et al., 2011) fpr a tptal mass of ~109 MDa (Reichelt et al., 1990).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: FG-nups contain repeat motifs of phenylalanine-glycine that interact with cargo and its chaperones.
source: These are known as 'FG-nups' because they contain repeat motifs of phenylalanine-glycine that interact with cargo and its chaperones, known as the importins, exportins, or karyopherins (kaps).
evidence: This is established knowledge about FG-nup structure and function.

claim: Differential expression levels and stoichiometries of Nups are observed between different cell types.
source: Differential expression levels (D'Angelo et al., 2012; Lupu et al., 2008) and stoichiometries (Ori et al., 2013) of Nups are observed between different cell types.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Different Nups within the mammalian NPC have different residence times.
source: Furthermore, within the mammalian NPC, different Nups have been shown to have different residence times, which has led to the suggestion that those with shorter residence times may serve adaptor or regulatory functions (Rabut et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Nups with shorter residence times may serve adaptor or regulatory functions.
source: Furthermore, within the mammalian NPC, different Nups have been shown to have different residence times, which has led to the suggestion that those with shorter residence times may serve adaptor or regulatory functions (Rabut et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from the literature supported by citation.

claim: The additional mass of the mammalian NPC exists in the absence of substantial changes to the size of the central channel.
source: The additional mass of the mammalian NPC exists in the absence of substantial changes to the size of the central channel, raising the possibility that the mammalian NPC is subject to additional regulation.
evidence: This is an observation that leads to speculation about NPC regulation.

claim: The mammalian NPC may be subject to additional regulation.
source: The additional mass of the mammalian NPC exists in the absence of substantial changes to the size of the central channel, raising the possibility that the mammalian NPC is subject to additional regulation.
evidence: This is speculation based on structural observations.

claim: In adherent cell lines used in this study, the nuclei tend to be flattened ovoids.
source: In the adherent cell lines used in this study, the nuclei tend to be flattened ovoids and the NPCs on the basal surface share a common orientation with their central axis perpendicular to the coverslip.
evidence: This is an observation about the experimental system used in the study.

claim: NPCs on the basal surface share a common orientation with their central axis perpendicular to the coverslip.
source: In the adherent cell lines used in this study, the nuclei tend to be flattened ovoids and the NPCs on the basal surface share a common orientation with their central axis perpendicular to the coverslip.
evidence: This is an observation about the experimental system that enables the pol-TIRFM approach.

claim: Each component of the NPC is in 8-fold symmetry.
source: Since each component of the NPC is in 8-fold symmetry, it is a compelling test structure to assay conformational changes in vivo.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about NPCs.

claim: Polarized-total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy (pol-TIRFM) was used to monitor the orientation of mEGFP-based sensors incorporated into different domains of individual NPCs in living cells.
source: Using polarized-total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy (pol-TIRFM), we monitored the orientation of mEGFP-based sensors incorporated into different domains of individual NPCs in living cells.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: Fluorescence anisotropy was previously used to determine the organization of the Y-shaped complex with respect to the NPC.
source: Previously, to measure the organization of various Nups with respect to the NPC we used fluorescence anisotropy. We determined the organization of the Y-shaped complex with respect to the NPC (Kampmann et al., 2011) and characterized the orientations and rigidity of the FG-Nup domains (Atkinson et al., 2013; Mattheyses et al., 2010).
evidence: This describes previous work by the authors supported by citations.

claim: Fluorescence anisotropy was previously used to characterize the orientations and rigidity of the FG-Nup domains.
source: Previously, to measure the organization of various Nups with respect to the NPC we used fluorescence anisotropy. We determined the organization of the Y-shaped complex with respect to the NPC (Kampmann et al., 2011) and characterized the orientations and rigidity of the FG-Nup domains (Atkinson et al., 2013; Mattheyses et al., 2010).
evidence: This describes previous work by the authors supported by citations.

claim: The conformation of the inner ring of the NPC is modulated by both transport state and specific transport factors.
source: In this study, we examine the orientation of components of the scaffold and establish that the conformation of the inner ring of the NPC is modulated by both transport state and specific transport factors.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Orientational sensors were built by rigidly attaching mEGFP to different Nup domains.
source: To monitor conformational changes in the scaffold of the NPC, we built orientational sensors by rigidly attaching mEGFP to different Nup domains.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach of the study.

claim: The alpha helix at the amino terminus of mEGFP was conjugated to the carboxyl terminus of a Nup domain.
source: We conjugated the alpha helix at the amino terminus of mEGFP to the carboxyl terminus of a Nup domain.
evidence: This describes the specific design of the orientational sensors.

claim: The orientation of mEGFP is fixed to that of the Nup when rigidly conjugated.
source: Thus, the orientation of mEGFP is fixed to that of the Nup.
evidence: This is a design principle of the orientational sensors.

claim: The orientation of mEGFP can be monitored because the excitation dipole is fixed within the molecule.
source: The orientation of mEGFP can be monitored because the excitation dipole is fixed within the molecule.
evidence: This is a physical property of mEGFP that enables the measurement approach.

claim: The strength of mEGFP excitation is proportional to cos2(Θ), where Θ is the angle between the excitation light and the excitation dipole.
source: The strength of mEGFP excitation is proportional to cos2(Θ), where Θ is the angle between the excitation light and the excitation dipole.
evidence: This is a physical principle underlying the measurement technique.

claim: The fluorophore was excited sequentially with light polarized in two orthogonal directions to monitor the orientation of mEGFP.
source: To monitor the orientation of the mEGFP, we excited the fluorophore sequentially with light polarized in two orthogonal directions.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Total internal reflection (TIR) was used to restrict excitation to the basal surface of the cell.
source: To restrict excitation to the basal surface of the cell we created the two polarized fields using excitation by total internal reflection (TIR).
evidence: This describes a technical aspect of the experimental approach.

claim: The basal nuclear envelope is parallel to the coverslip.
source: Because the basal nuclear envelope is parallel to our coverslip, the NPCs embedded in the nuclear envelope are oriented relative to the optical axis of our microscope.
evidence: This is an observation about the experimental system.

claim: The orientation of Nups within individual NPCs in living cells can be monitored.
source: Therefore, we could monitor the orientation of Nups within individual NPCs in living cells.
evidence: This is a capability enabled by the experimental approach.

claim: A rearrangement of the structural core of the NPC occurs in response to manipulations of transport through the NPC.
source: Our results show a rearrangement of the structural core of the NPC, in particular of the inner ring Nups, in response to manipulations of transport through the NPC.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Light emitted from each Nup orientational sensor was measured in response to the two orthogonal polarizations of TIRF illumination.
source: We then measured the light emitted from each Nup orientational sensor in response to the two orthogonal polarizations of TIRF illumination (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the measurement approach, with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Orientational sensors were probed in Nup133, Nup93, Nup54, and Nup58.
source: We probed for conformational changes in the NPC with orientational sensors in Nup133, Nup93, Nup54, and Nup58.
evidence: This describes which Nups were studied.

claim: Nup133 is a member of the Y-shaped complex, which forms two reticulated rings at both the nuclear and cytoplasmic faces of the NPC.
source: Nup133 is a member of the Y-shaped complex, which forms two reticulated rings at both the nuclear and cytoplasmic faces of the NPC (Bui et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Nup93 is a member of the Nup93 complex (along with Nup205, Nup188, Nup155, and Nup53).
source: Nup93 is a member of the Nup93 complex (along with Nup205, Nup188, Nup155, and Nup53) and Nup54 and Nup58 are members of the Nup62 complex (along with Nup62).
evidence: This is established knowledge about NPC composition.

claim: Nup54 and Nup58 are members of the Nup62 complex (along with Nup62).
source: Nup93 is a member of the Nup93 complex (along with Nup205, Nup188, Nup155, and Nup53) and Nup54 and Nup58 are members of the Nup62 complex (along with Nup62).
evidence: This is established knowledge about NPC composition.

claim: Both the Nup93 and Nup62 complexes localize to the inner ring.
source: Both the Nup93 and Nup62 complexes localize to the inner ring (Vollmer and Antonin, 2014), between the two reticulated rings of Y-shaped complexes.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The Nup93 complex is embedded within the NPC scaffold.
source: The Nup93 complex is embedded within the NPC scaffold, and the Nup62 complex sits adjacent, closer to the lumen of the nuclear pore (Kosinski et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The Nup62 complex sits adjacent to the Nup93 complex, closer to the lumen of the nuclear pore.
source: The Nup93 complex is embedded within the NPC scaffold, and the Nup62 complex sits adjacent, closer to the lumen of the nuclear pore (Kosinski et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Orientational sensors were localized to three different structural positions within the NPC.
source: Therefore, our orientational sensors were localized to three different structural positions within the NPC (Figure 1C).
evidence: This describes the experimental design with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: Plasmids encoding putative orientational sensors were engineered to encode each Nup fused via an alpha helix to mEGFP.
source: Plasmids encoding putative orientational sensors were engineered to encode each Nup fused via an alpha helix to mEGFP.
evidence: This describes the molecular cloning approach.

claim: The first four amino acids of mEGFP were removed because they are not resolved in the crystal structure, suggesting that they are not rigid.
source: We removed the first four amino acids of the mEGFP because they are not resolved in the crystal structure, suggesting that they are not rigid.
evidence: This describes a design decision based on structural information.

claim: The distribution of total intensities of the puncta observed was only a single peak indicating detection of individual NPCs.
source: With an algorithm that uses a Laplacian of blob-detection method (Pulupa, 2020) the distribution of total intensities of the puncta observed was only a single peak indicating we are detecting individual NPCs.
evidence: This is a validation of the detection method.

claim: If the mEGFP is rigidly conjugated to a Nup that is properly incorporated into the NPC, then changes of the p:s ratio represent changes in orientation of the domain of the Nup to which the mEGFP is conjugated.
source: If the mEGFP is rigidly conjugated to a Nup that is properly incorporated into the NPC, then changes of the p:s ratio represent changes in orientation of the domain of the Nup to which the mEGFP is conjugated.
evidence: This is a logical inference about what the measurement reports.

claim: Changing the length of the alpha-helical linker by a single amino acid should rotate the mEGFP ~103° around the axis of the alpha helix if the mEGFP is held rigidly relative to a Nup.
source: If the mEGFP is held rigidly relative to a Nup, then changing the length of the alpha-helical linker by a single amino acid should rotate the mEGFP ~103° around the axis of the alpha helix.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the geometry of alpha helices.

claim: The p:s ratio should shift with the number of amino acids in the linker if the reporter is a proxy for the orientation of the Nup.
source: Therefore, if our reporter is a proxy for the orientation of the Nup, the p:s ratio should shift with the number of amino acids in the linker.
evidence: This is a prediction that serves as a validation criterion.

claim: The p:s ratio shifted with different lengths of the rigid linkers, confirming that the dipole of the mEGFP is a proxy for the orientation of the Nup54.
source: The p:s ratio shifted with different lengths of the rigid linkers, confirming that the dipole of the mEGFP is a proxy for the orientation of the Nup54 (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a validation result supported by data in Figure 1F.

claim: No difference in p:s ratio was observed with varying lengths of the flexible linkers.
source: No difference in p:s ratio was observed with varying lengths of the flexible linkers (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is a control result supported by data in Figure 1G.

claim: Orientational sensors are considered functional if the p:s ratio shifts upon the addition of a single amino acid.
source: Thus, we developed a criterion whereby orientational sensors are considered functional if the p:s ratio shifts upon the addition of a single amino acid.
evidence: This describes the validation criterion for the sensors.

claim: Functional orientational sensors were confirmed with mEGFP conjugated to Nup133, Nup93, Nup58, and Nup54.
source: Using this criterion, we confirmed that we have orientational sensors with mEGFP conjugated to Nup133, Nup93, Nup58, and Nup54 (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is a validation result supported by data in Figure 2A-D.

claim: Distinct shifts in the p:s ratio were seen when constructs differed by a single amino acid for Nup133, Nup93, Nup58, and Nup54.
source: We saw distinct shifts in the p:s ratio when constructs differed by a single amino acid.
evidence: This is a validation result for the orientational sensors.

claim: The p:s ratio did not change upon rotating the linker alpha helix when mEGFP was placed at the carboxyl terminus of Nup54.
source: An exception was when mEGFP was placed at the carboxyl terminus of Nup54. This domain is currently unresolved in any crystal structure, and the p:s ratio did not change upon rotating the linker alpha helix (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a negative result supported by data in Figure 2E.

claim: The carboxyl terminus domain of Nup54 is not held rigidly.
source: This indicates that this domain of Nup54 is not held rigidly, consistent with the inability to crystallize this domain of the protein and suggests the carboxyl terminus is a flexible domain.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental result and structural knowledge.

claim: The carboxyl terminus of Nup54 is a flexible domain.
source: This indicates that this domain of Nup54 is not held rigidly, consistent with the inability to crystallize this domain of the protein and suggests the carboxyl terminus is a flexible domain.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental result.

claim: Variations in the p:s ratio in different NPCs were not detected with respect to position along the basal surface of the nucleus.
source: For any specific Nup-mEGFP, variations in the p:s ratio in different NPCs were not detected with respect to position along the basal surface of the nucleus (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), indicating a shared orientation for these NPCs.
evidence: This is an observation supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: NPCs on the basal surface of the nucleus share a common orientation.
source: For any specific Nup-mEGFP, variations in the p:s ratio in different NPCs were not detected with respect to position along the basal surface of the nucleus (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), indicating a shared orientation for these NPCs.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that p:s ratios do not vary with position.

claim: In yeast, starvation inhibits the import of cargo with nuclear localization sequences.
source: In yeast, starvation inhibits the import of cargo with nuclear localization sequences, or NLS-tagged cargo (Stochaj et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature supported by citation.

claim: The rates of nucleo-cytoplasmic trafficking were attenuated after starvation.
source: We confirmed the rates of nucleo-cytoplasmic trafficking were attenuated using a photoactivatable nuclear transport cargo (Yumerefendi et al., 2015; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a validation result supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: After starvation there were no detectable changes in the orientations of Nup133 and Nup93.
source: After starvation there were no detectable changes in the orientations of Nup133 and Nup93 (Figure 3A–B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is an experimental result supported by data in Figure 3A-B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-D.

claim: The NPC retains its orientation relative to the coverslip after starvation.
source: These results are consistent with the NPC retaining its orientation relative to the coverslip.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that Nup133 and Nup93 orientations do not change.

claim: The nuclear envelope is not distorted post-starvation.
source: The consistency across the basal surface of the nucleus shows the nuclear envelope is not distorted post-starvation.
evidence: This is an inference from the consistency of measurements across the nucleus.

claim: Conformational reporters Nup58 and amino acid 494 in Nup54 exhibited significant shifts post-starvation.
source: In contrast, conformational reporters Nup58 and amino acid 494 in Nup54 (Nup54-mEGFP494, or Nup54494) exhibited significant shifts post-starvation (Figure 3C–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–H).
evidence: This is a primary experimental result supported by data in Figure 3C-D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2E-H.

claim: Orientational shifts in select alpha helices of Nup54 and Nup58 reflect a reorganization of these inner ring Nups relative to the NPC.
source: These orientational shifts in select alpha helices of Nup54 and Nup58 reflected a reorganization of these inner ring Nups relative to the NPC.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: The orientation shift of Nup54494 was also seen in Nup54 orientational sensors where the FG-Nup domain was eliminated.
source: The orientation shift of Nup54494 was also seen in Nup54 orientational sensors where the FG-Nup domain was eliminated (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an experimental result supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Orientational changes in Nup54 are propagated throughout the inner ring, independent of whether the individual Nup54 polypeptide containing the orientational sensor is bound to a kap.
source: This result suggests that these orientational changes are propagated throughout the inner ring, independent of whether the individual Nup54 polypeptide containing the orientational sensor is bound to a kap.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the result with the FG-domain deleted construct.

claim: No shift was observed in the reporter at amino acid 510 in Nup54 (the carboxyl terminus) after starvation.
source: No shift was observed in the previously described reporter at amino acid 510 in Nup54 (Nup54-mEGFP510, or Nup54510), the carboxyl terminus (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is an experimental result supported by data in Figure 3E.

claim: There is a change of orientation of select alpha-helical domains of Nup58 and Nup54 in the absence of a change in the orientation of the rest of the NPC.
source: These results suggest a change of orientation of select alpha-helical domains of Nup58 and Nup54 in the absence of a change in the orientation of the rest of the NPC.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the combined experimental results.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 was used to create cell lines in which both endogenous copies of either Nup133 or Nup54 are replaced with their fluorescent orientational sensor equivalent.
source: To ensure that the Nup-mEGFP fusion proteins are functional and to improve the signal to noise, we used CRISPR/Cas9 to create cell lines in which both endogenous copies of either Nup133 or Nup54 are replaced with their fluorescent orientational sensor equivalent.
evidence: This describes the generation of CRISPR cell lines.

claim: The CRISPR cell lines are homozygous.
source: We confirmed that these cell lines are homozygous (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and observed no changes in cell growth or morphology (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is a validation result supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: No changes in cell growth or morphology were observed in the CRISPR cell lines.
source: We confirmed that these cell lines are homozygous (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and observed no changes in cell growth or morphology (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is a validation result supported by data in Figure 4A-B.

claim: Single amino acid alterations in the linker length shifted the p:s ratio in the CRISPR cell lines.
source: These cell lines also shared the property that single amino acid alterations in the linker length shifted the p:s ratio (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This is a validation result supported by data in Figure 4C-D.

claim: The Nup133 and Nup54 CRISPR cell lines exhibit similar p:s ratios to the transient transfections.
source: The Nup133 and Nup54 CRISPR cell lines exhibit similar p:s ratios to the transient transfections.
evidence: This is a comparison between CRISPR and transfection results.

claim: A difference in the p:s ratio of a little above one in the Nup133 CRISPR cell lines and below one in the transient transfections was measured.
source: However, we measure a difference in the p:s ratio of a little above one in the Nup133 CRISPR cell lines and below one in the transient transfections.
evidence: This is an observation of a difference between experimental conditions.

claim: The difference in p:s ratio between CRISPR and transfection may reflect a slight alteration in NPC structure between two different cell types or is a methodological consequence.
source: This difference may reflect a slight alteration in NPC structure between two different cell types or is a methodological consequence of either variable incorporation levels of fluorescent Nup133 in the transient transfection or the higher background fluorescence in the transient transfection, which might slightly lower the ratio from above 1 to below 1.
evidence: This is speculation about the cause of the observed difference.

claim: When starved, the CRISPR cell lines mimicked the results of the transiently transfected cell lines.
source: When starved, the CRISPR cell lines mimicked the results of the transiently transfected cell lines (Figure 4E–F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2); the orientation of Nup54494 exhibited a significant change but the orientation of the Nup133 did not shift after starvation.
evidence: This is an experimental result supported by data in Figure 4E-F and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The orientation of Nup54494 exhibited a significant change after starvation in CRISPR cell lines.
source: When starved, the CRISPR cell lines mimicked the results of the transiently transfected cell lines (Figure 4E–F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2); the orientation of Nup54494 exhibited a significant change but the orientation of the Nup133 did not shift after starvation.
evidence: This is an experimental result supported by data in Figure 4E-F.

claim: The orientation of Nup133 did not shift after starvation in CRISPR cell lines.
source: When starved, the CRISPR cell lines mimicked the results of the transiently transfected cell lines (Figure 4E–F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2); the orientation of Nup54494 exhibited a significant change but the orientation of the Nup133 did not shift after starvation.
evidence: This is an experimental result supported by data in Figure 4E-F.

claim: Nup54 was reorganized when transport was reduced.
source: Just as in the transient transfections, Nup54 was reorganized when transport was reduced.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the starvation experiments.

claim: Digitonin can selectively permeabilize the plasma membrane while leaving the nuclear membrane intact at a certain concentration.
source: At a certain concentration, digitonin can selectively permeabilize the plasma membrane while leaving the nuclear membrane intact, resulting in the loss of many cytoplasmic components and the cessation of nuclear-cytoplasmic trafficking (Adam et al., 1992).
evidence: This is established knowledge about digitonin permeabilization supported by citation.

claim: Digitonin permeabilization results in the loss of many cytoplasmic components and the cessation of nuclear-cytoplasmic trafficking.
source: At a certain concentration, digitonin can selectively permeabilize the plasma membrane while leaving the nuclear membrane intact, resulting in the loss of many cytoplasmic components and the cessation of nuclear-cytoplasmic trafficking (Adam et al., 1992).
evidence: This is established knowledge about digitonin permeabilization supported by citation.

claim: The nuclear envelope remained intact after digitonin permeabilization.
source: After digitonin permeabilization, we monitored cells to ensure that the nuclear envelope remained intact (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) and we confirmed that the cells were capable of translocating specific NLS-tagged cargos (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: This is a validation result supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Permeabilized cells were capable of translocating specific NLS-tagged cargos.
source: After digitonin permeabilization, we monitored cells to ensure that the nuclear envelope remained intact (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) and we confirmed that the cells were capable of translocating specific NLS-tagged cargos (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: This is a validation result supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-E.

claim: A distinct shift in the orientation of Nup54494 was observed compared to the orientation of Nup54494 in unpermeabilized cells grown in complete media when cells were permeabilized and incubated in transport buffer plus 1.5% (wt/vol) 360kD polyvinylpyrrolidone.
source: When we permeabilize cells and incubate in transport buffer plus 1.5% (wt/vol) 360kD polyvinylpyrrolidone to mimic cytosolic conditions, we observed a distinct shift in the orientation of Nup54494 compared to the orientation of Nup54494 in unpermeabilized cells grown in complete media.
evidence: This is an experimental result.

claim: No change in the orientation of Nup133 was seen in permeabilized cells compared to Nup133 in unpermeabilized cells grown in complete media.
source: We saw no change in the orientation of Nup133 in permeabilized cells compared to Nup133 in unpermeabilized cells grown in complete media (Figure 4G–H).
evidence: This is an experimental result supported by data in Figure 4G-H.

claim: Leptomycin B blocks nuclear export by inhibiting crm1 (exportin-1).
source: Leptomycin B blocks nuclear export by inhibiting crm1 (exportin-1), an evolutionarily conserved export factor (Kudo et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge about leptomycin B supported by citation.

claim: An orientational shift of Nup54494 was observed after treatment with 25 nM leptomycin B for 15 hr.
source: We treated our cells with 25 nM leptomycin B for 15 hr and observed an orientational shift of Nup54494 but no change to the orientation of Nup133 (Figure 4I–J).
evidence: This is an experimental result supported by data in Figure 4I-J.

claim: No change to the orientation of Nup133 was observed after treatment with leptomycin B.
source: We treated our cells with 25 nM leptomycin B for 15 hr and observed an orientational shift of Nup54494 but no change to the orientation of Nup133 (Figure 4I–J).
evidence: This is an experimental result supported by data in Figure 4I-J.

claim: Ran is a GTPase that mediates nuclear transport.
source: Ran is a GTPase that mediates nuclear transport (Moore and Blobel, 1993).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Ran supported by citation.

claim: Ran undergoes GTP-hydrolysis in the cytosol that causes the Ran-Kap1-β export complex to dissociate from the NPCs, thereby replenishing Kap1-β in the cytosol.
source: Ran undergoes GTP- hydrolysis in the cytosol that causes the Ran-Kap1-β export complex to dissociate from the NPCs, thereby replenishing Kap1-β in the cytosol.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Ran cycle.

claim: Ran-Q69L is a dominant-negative mutant that cannot perform GTP-hydrolysis, thereby blocking Ran-dependent import and export.
source: Ran-Q69L is a dominant-negative mutant that cannot perform GTP-hydrolysis, thereby blocking Ran-dependent import and export (Bischoff et al., 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Ran-Q69L mutant supported by citation.

claim: Cells transiently expressing BFP-RanQ69L for 24 hr were not capable of nuclear-cytoplasmic trafficking.
source: We confirmed that cells transiently expressing BFP-RanQ69L for 24 hr were not capable of nuclear-cytoplasmic trafficking by using a light induced nuclear shuttle (Figure 4M–N).
evidence: This is a validation result supported by data in Figure 4M-N.

claim: Nup54494 was rearranged with respect to the NPC after cells were transfected with a dominant-negative Ran.
source: Nup54494 was rearranged once again with respect to the NPC but the Nup133 did not change orientation after cells were transfected with a dominant-negative Ran (Figure 4K–L).
evidence: This is an experimental result supported by data in Figure 4K-L.

claim: Nup133 did not change orientation after cells were transfected with a dominant-negative Ran.

claim: The Ring Cycle hypothesis suggests that the structured regions of inner ring Nups cycle between a dilated ring of 40–50 nm in diameter and a constricted ring of 20 nm in diameter.
source: Structural studies based on two discrete crystal states of short peptides of three inner channel ring Nups, Nup58, Nup54, and Nup62, have led to the proposal that the structured regions of these inner ring Nups cycle between a dilated ring of 40–50 nm in diameter and a constricted ring of 20 nm in diameter. This Ring Cycle hypothesis suggests that this ring undergoes conformational changes and directly regulates cargo import and export (Melcák et al., 2007; Sharma et al., 2015; Solmaz et al., 2013; Solmaz et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from the literature supported by multiple citations.
